ImageDescription.value: A macro of soap bubbles (more accurately foam I think) processed through Lightroom and Silver Efex Pro.  The photos were taken in my DIY light box.  I noticed some rather unusual bubbles on a brush used to clean a blender in which a protein shake had been made.  The brush had been in the sink for some time and the bubbles were still formed so i decided to do some macro photography.  The second photo is not a macro that gives a better idea of the clump of bubbles.

ImageDescription.value:
This image shows a lamp's reflection on a soap bubble, revealing a vibrant rainbow pattern resulting from thin film interference. This phenomenon occurs when white light interacts with a thin film, causing partial reflection and refraction. As the light reaches the film's opposite side, it is again partially reflected and refracted. The two reflected light portions then converge and interfere, leading to either constructive or destructive interference under specific conditions. Due to distinct frequencies of different colors, interference varies, and the film's uneven thickness across the bubble allows for diverse constructive interference, forming the rainbow effect. This occurrence is also visible in other thin films, such as oil on water and glass coatings.
To capture this image, a 1:3 dishwashing soap and water mixture was created, with added glycerin to enhance surface tension and  prevent the bubble from popping. The final image was cropped without further adjustments. SONY ILCE-6400, 30mm Macro Lens, 1/500s, f/22, ISO 1000.
